text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The paper's editorial calls on Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi to resign, alleging his government was unable to handle the crisis sparked by the collapse of dubious pyramid investment schemes.
- Some 80,000 people attended the funeral of an anti-government demonstrator killed in the southern town of Vlore during violent clashes between riot police and protesters on Monday.
- Thousands of residents of the southern town of Fieri marched on foot to join protesters in Vlore on Monday. Peaceful rallies were reported from across the country.
- After police abandoned Vlore, residents reclaim some 135 speed boats seized by police over the past weeks in an attempt to curb illegal trade.
- Main opposition Socialist Party accuses President Sali Berisha of provoking a civil war by refusing to dismiss his government and call for the installation of a "technocrat government".
- Meksi's government was effectively "toppled" in Vlore, the paper says.
- Some key members of the ruling Democratic Party opposed to Meksi call for emergency rule to be introduced in Vlore.
- The right-wing Republican Party has withdrawn its support for Berisha's government and calls for early elections.

- The collapse of pyramid investment schemes and the protests sparked by the crisis are a threat to neighbouring Greece, which is worried about a potential wave of immigrants from its impoverished northern neighbour.
- The main opposition Democratic Forum alliance has called for an anti-government rally in Tirana at midday on Wednesday.
- The ruling Democratic Party blames the Italian mafia for the spread of pyramid schemes in Albania.
- European states are eager to help Albania overcome its political and economic crisis and to prevent communists from returning to power.
